text:
alex: Rolling NVIDIA 535.86 -> 536.25 to CANARY nodes in us-east-1 started at 11:02. Quick heads-up: we're seeing NCCL watchdog spikes and a handful of Xid 31/4 in the canary group. Posting here so infra is aware.

eng_ops_bot: ALERT: nccl_watchdog_rate{group="canary",region="us-east-1"} > 5/min (see dashboard https://dash.redwood/internal/nccl-watchdog)

marta: Seeing correlated nv_peer_mem messages and a kernel oops on gpu-canary-07. `kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31` repeated.

priya: Can we pause the rollout and pin back to 535.86 on canary? What's the rollback command for the driver package?

alex: Pausing rollout now. Command to pause: `./deployctl rollout --env=prod --group=canary --pause`
Rollback (deb/apt env): `sudo dpkg -i /opt/drivers/nvidia-535.86.deb && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-gpu.service`
I'll coordinate manual rollbacks on affected canary nodes.

josh: Uploaded full kernel logs + gdb stacks to s3: s3://redwood-gpu-logs/1965432100/stacktraces.tar.gz. Also captured nvml traces.

infra-oncall: :eyes: Opening P1 ticket now and running the collection script across canary nodes. Starting rollback on 01-08 in sequence to avoid mass resets.

marta: Noted: three nodes showed immediate GPU reset during driver revert (Xid 31). Logging that in the P1.

priya: We should tweak the alert to reduce noise. Proposal: require sustained errors and multi-node impact. Example PromQL: `sum_over_time(nccl_watchdog_errors{region="us-east-1",group="canary"}[3m]) > 3 and count_values("node", nccl_watchdog_errors{...}) > 1` — open to wording.

alex: Agree. Also saw higher incidence on long-sequence workloads (90+ tokens), might be interacting with kernel page pinning. Can we tag sequence length in the request metrics?

eng_ops_bot: Runbook link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/nccl-watchdog. Suggested edits: add explicit rollback steps, add "suppress for N minutes" guidance, and include the diagnostic commands below.

josh: I'll open a PR to update the runbook + the alert rule. Plan: 1) Pause global rollout, 2) Revert canary drivers, 3) Run a compatibility test suite across heterogenous kernels, 4) Only resume after 12h stable canary. ETA: PR in ~1.5h.

infra-oncall: Rollback progress: 4/8 canary nodes reverted so far. No new Xid spikes on those 4. Remaining nodes queued.

marta: Small ops/cost note: keeping canary roped to older driver for a day will slightly impact packing and could increase spot spend by ~0.2% — flagged for finance but not blocking.

priya: After rollback, we should add a staged rollout checklist: 1) smoke perf/correctness on 5 nodes (heterogeneous), 2) synthetic NCCL watchdog test (3m sustained), 3) 12h canary, 4) regional ramp with automated rollback triggers. I'll add to release checklist.

alex: Thanks everyone. Immediate next steps: finish canary rollback, update alert rule to require 3m sustained and multi-node, PR runbook edits, collect full traces, and start compatibility matrix run. I'll write a short postmortem after logs are analyzed. Channel set to P1 for now. :thumbsup:
